dmcs.dropped_lowest_ur_overlap.spec: states in BOTH dmcs.dropped_near_trigger_states and dmcs.lowest_mean_ur_states -- the '3 of 5' overlap Appendix 13.4 reports

dmcs.dropped_near_trigger_states.cross_check: dmcs.py main(): set(df.columns) - set(dmcs.csv's state column)
dmcs.dropped_near_trigger_states.spec: states with a long enough UR panel to attempt the near-trigger decision-loss comparison but dropped by year_mcs's len(M)<30 floor once restricted to near-trigger months -- the 'excluded 7' Appendix 13.4 names

cites: S7 body: exactly equal in 18 states
dmcs.equal_symmetric.spec: states where the decision-loss |MCS| is EXACTLY equal to the near-trigger statistical |MCS| (matched T) -- the 'as wide but not wider' half of dmcs.tied_both_symmetric's never-narrower finding

dmcs.lowest_mean_ur_states.spec: the 5 states with the lowest mean unemployment rate over the full UR panel (all 51 jurisdictions, unfiltered) -- compared against dmcs.dropped_near_trigger_states in Appendix 13.4 to show the excluded set is related to, but not identical to, the lowest-UR states

dmcs.mean_set_decision.spec: mean |MCS| across states under the DECISION loss (misclassification of the realized EB trigger status), alpha=0.10, measured ONLY on near-trigger months (near-trigger months only, not the full sample, which is dominated by the trivial always-off region). T-ASYMMETRY NOTE, RESOLVED: this leg runs on a median 9 near-trigger YEARS per state (distinct calendar years among the near-trigger months, range 5-21; read from dmcs.csv's near_trigger_years column) vs. dmcs.mean_set_statistical's median 36 years -- a real T-asymmetry between the two MCS legs dmcs.separates/dmcs.tied_both compare directly, raising the concern that a high mean |MCS| here could be an artifact of the shorter-T leg eliminating fewer candidates almost mechanically. Resolved by dmcs.mean_set_statistical_near (the statistical MCS recomputed at matched T): see dmcs.tied_both_symmetric, which is identical to dmcs.tied_both under matched T -- the T-asymmetry was not the explanation.

dmcs.mean_set_statistical.spec: mean |MCS| across states under the STATISTICAL loss (absolute nowcast error), alpha=0.10, over the FULL scored sample (only the decision loss below is restricted to near-trigger months)

dmcs.mean_set_statistical_near.spec: mean |MCS| across states under the STATISTICAL loss, alpha=0.10, restricted to the SAME near-trigger months as dmcs.mean_set_decision (matched T) -- the symmetric counterpart to dmcs.mean_set_statistical's full-sample figure, added to isolate whether dmcs.tied_both reflects genuine ambiguity or the T-asymmetry between the two full-sample-vs-near-trigger legs

dmcs.n_eligible.cross_check: dmcs.py main(): count of states with len(u) >= 300
dmcs.n_eligible.spec: states with a long enough UR panel (>=300 months) to even ATTEMPT the comparison, before the near-trigger floor -- disclosed so dmcs.n_states' drop from this is not silent

dmcs.n_states.spec: number of states retained after BOTH floors: a long enough UR panel (>=300 months) AND enough near-trigger months for year_mcs's existing len(M)<30 floor to run the decision-loss MCS meaningfully

dmcs.separates.spec: states where the near-trigger-only decision loss produces a STRICTLY smaller tied set than the (full-sample) statistical loss (the tie dissolves when selecting on the decision that actually matters, measured where it can actually discriminate)

cites: S7 body: no cell shows a narrower decision-loss |MCS| than accuracy-loss |MCS|
dmcs.separates_symmetric.spec: states where the near-trigger decision loss produces a strictly smaller tied set than the near-trigger STATISTICAL loss (matched T on both legs) -- the symmetric counterpart to dmcs.separates, which compares against the full-sample statistical loss instead

dmcs.single_decision.spec: states where the near-trigger-only decision-loss tied set is a singleton (the decision loss fully identifies a winner even restricted to the months where it can discriminate)

dmcs.tied_both.spec: states where the tied set under the near-trigger-only decision loss is NOT smaller than under the (full-sample) statistical loss AND still has more than one admissible model -- candidate reading: genuine ambiguity even where the decision loss has the best chance to discriminate, reported as a confidence set of admissible statutory actions rather than a point call. T-ASYMMETRY CHECK (see dmcs.mean_set_decision): dMCS_decision >= MCS_stat in EVERY retained state raised the concern that this could be an artifact of the T-asymmetry between the two MCS legs (near-trigger-restricted vs. full-sample) rather than genuine information. Resolved: dmcs.tied_both_symmetric (the same comparison at matched T) is IDENTICAL, 44/44 vs 44/44 -- even though the underlying per-state statistical-MCS sizes genuinely differ between the full-sample and near-trigger-restricted legs in 27 of 44 states (confirming the T-restriction is not a no-op), the decision loss is at least as broad as the statistical loss either way, in every state.

dmcs.tied_both_symmetric.spec: states where the tied set under the near-trigger decision loss is not smaller than under the near-trigger STATISTICAL loss (matched T on both legs) AND still has more than one admissible model -- the symmetric counterpart to dmcs.tied_both, which compares against the full-sample statistical loss instead. Compare directly against dmcs.tied_both: if the two counts agree, the T-asymmetry was not the explanation for dmcs.tied_both and it can be cited as genuine ambiguity; if they diverge, the T-asymmetry was inflating dmcs.tied_both and this matched-T figure is the one to cite instead

cites: S7 body: decision loss manufactures ambiguity from a clean statistical winner
dmcs.wider_from_singleton.spec: of dmcs.wider_symmetric's states (decision-loss |MCS| strictly wider than near-trigger statistical |MCS|), how many started from MCS_stat_near==1 -- a CLEAN, unambiguous statistical winner with zero pre-existing tie. For these states the decision rule does not widen an existing ambiguity, it manufactures a new one from a previously clean identification. tied_both/wider_symmetric do not distinguish this case from a genuinely-tied statistical set growing wider still -- both fall under the same 'genuine ambiguity' framing; this key separates them.

cites: S7 body: singleton under the full-sample statistical comparison too
dmcs.wider_from_singleton_also_full_samp.spec: of dmcs.wider_from_singleton's states (decision-loss |MCS| strictly wider than the near-trigger-restricted statistical |MCS|, MCS_stat_near==1), how many are ALSO a singleton under the FULL-SAMPLE statistical comparison (MCS_stat==1) -- i.e. not just a clean winner once restricted to near-trigger months, but a clean winner under the unrestricted full-sample MCS too

cites: S7 body: strictly wider in the remaining states
dmcs.wider_symmetric.spec: states where the decision-loss |MCS| is STRICTLY wider than the near-trigger statistical |MCS| (matched T) -- the complementary half of dmcs.equal_symmetric; equal_symmetric + wider_symmetric + narrower_symmetric (always 0, see dmcs.tied_both_symmetric) must sum to n
